parallel.requirements: Recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering task: infer behavior only by running the supplied executable and reading bundled docs, then produce an original executable-compatible codebase without wrapping or external source.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent read docs, created broad todos, launched a workflow fan-out over seven behavioral probe areas plus critique/gap-fill passes, and also launched an extra child to derive parser rule order.
parallel.implementation: The run created a Rust project and worked on a PEG/parser support module, with a late edit to src/peg.rs, but it did not complete the shell implementation or main entry point.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted archive contained scaffolding such as Cargo.toml, compile.sh, and src/peg.rs, but no complete executable source tree or src/main.rs capable of compiling.
parallel.verification: Most verification effort was behavioral probing of the reference executable and notes collection; official evaluation later failed at compile time before running tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow and an extra child were stopped near timeout, several probes were in stalled retry states, and the final deliverable was incomplete and unbuildable.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering task and constraints, reading the documentation and probing only the provided binary.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single actor with workflow and task delegation disabled, repeatedly probing command-line behavior, shell constructs, builtins, arithmetic, and background jobs.
serial.implementation: Despite extensive probing, the serial run did not construct a replacement source project; the artifact remained dominated by original docs and the provided executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No integrated implementation was assembled or packaged as a buildable replacement; the submitted artifact did not include generated source analogous to a complete shell.
serial.verification: Serial verification consisted of local binary probes against the reference executable, followed by official compile failure with no tests run.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The single-actor attempt timed out after investigation and never delivered a compilable reimplementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the requirement to write a new original codebase from observed executable behavior and docs only.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the same reverse-engineering and no-wrapper constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference explains the official result; both failed despite starting from identical requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into seven workflow probe areas with per-area agents and critique/gap-fill followups, plus an extra parser-focused child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial remained single-actor with delegation disabled and no workflow children.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed investigation broadly; serial kept ownership centralized. The parallel split produced more evidence but also substantial coordination and retry overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed and task-specific, including behavioral probes and cleanup expectations, but shared HOME state leaked across actors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child interfaces or handoffs; context stayed within one process and protocol validation found no delegation or contamination paths.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context/interface difference is not missing brief content but the parallel run exposing actors to shared environment artifacts that serial could not create through delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel started an original Rust implementation and edited parser support late in the run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial focused on observing the existing executable and did not package a generated source implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel progressed further toward code artifacts, but not to a complete compiling shell; serial produced less implementation surface and also failed to build.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had workflow and extra child activity still being stopped at closure, so not all delegated results reached a usable final integration point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all probe observations stayed in the main actor stream.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unresolved delegated work at shutdown, whereas serial had no join problem but still no deliverable implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a shared workspace and shared HOME; one config probe created .nshrc and unrelated later probes consumed its startup output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial operated without delegation and protocol validation recorded no contamination path hits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered concrete environment contamination in probe evidence, while serial avoided cross-actor shared-state leakage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran extensive reference probes and collected notes, but no whole-task acceptance test succeeded; official evaluation failed during compile.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also relied on behavioral probes and likewise failed official evaluation at compile time with all tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked evaluator-aligned build acceptance before closure; parallel had more probe volume but not a compiling replacement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a 2400-second window with 32 subagents, more than 4.2 million tokens, and 1.3 million workflow-child tokens before return code 143.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with zero subagents and no workflow-child tokens, spending its budget on single-actor probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but parallel closure was shaped by workflow fan-out, stalls, and child stops; serial closure was ordinary single-actor incompletion.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations are not discordant: both the parallel and serial runs failed with compile_failed and 2,289 tests not run. The concrete task-solving difference is process shape, not pass/fail outcome: parallel gathered much broader distributed probe evidence and began a partial Rust source tree, while serial stayed in one actor and mostly probed the reference executable without creating a replacement source project. Neither delivered a complete compilable reimplementation.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out and repeated stalled retries consumed substantial budget before implementation and packaging were complete.
A shared HOME .nshrc created by one child contaminated later probes and forced another child to isolate HOME.
The submitted artifact contained only partial Rust scaffolding and no complete entry-point implementation.
serial_contributors: The single-actor run spent its budget on documentation and behavioral probes and did not assemble a replacement codebase.
The submitted serial artifact remained the original documentation/executable tree and failed compile evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel made a late parser-module edit; serial did not produce comparable generated source.
Both attempts lacked a buildable executable, so their common official failure is primarily incomplete implementation/delivery rather than an evaluator-only discrepancy.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference is claimed; retained labels describe realized adverse parallel process episodes supported by trajectory evidence.

candidates.reason: Rejected because the parallel parent and delegated children did own investigation and implementation work; the failure was budget exhaustion and incompleteness, not absence of any implementer.
Rejected because there were no completed independently owned components needing an unowned reconciliation step; the run did not reach a mature multi-component integration boundary.
Rejected because the parent did create project scaffolding and compile machinery, while the missing final artifact followed from unfinished implementation rather than no named assembly owner.
Rejected because the parent/workflow owned the end-to-end probe-to-implementation pipeline even though it exhausted time; ownership itself was not absent.
Rejected because no single mandatory preflight blocked otherwise ready implementation; the broad probe workflow and retries, not one gate, consumed budget.
Rejected because the parallel trajectory interleaved parent implementation work with active workflow probing rather than completing investigation as a fully separate serial phase.
Rejected as a less specific description of the retained broad fan-out and retry episode; the evidence shows collective breadth exhaustion rather than only underallocation to one path.

The workflow launched a broad probe pipeline and then repeatedly retried stalled probe agents. Near closure it had accumulated more than a million workflow tokens and hundreds of tool uses, the workflow was stopped, and the archive still lacked a complete buildable shell implementation.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation and packaging work was displaced by the broad probe/retry workflow, leaving only a partial Rust project in the submitted archive.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent observed workflow progress and stopped active work; the defining boundary was collective fan-out and retry budget exhaustion, not a passive wait without inspection.

candidates.reason: Rejected because no single child assignment is the dominant overbroad scope responsible for the consequence; multiple probe areas and retries collectively consumed budget.
Rejected because the retained failures do not turn on a known requirement missing from a child brief; probe briefs included the relevant behavioral and artifact constraints.
Rejected because no incompatible separately produced components or omitted interoperation contract are shown as the concrete failure; most work remained probe notes or a partial single Rust module.
Rejected because no known finding is shown disappearing between actors and causing repeated work; stalled retries were a budget/lifecycle symptom rather than proven transferred information loss.
Rejected because available child notes or progress were not shown to be too large for the parent to consume; the run was still budget-limited before complete handoff reduction.
Rejected because no receiver is shown relying on superseded workspace or requirement state to make an invalid next step.
Rejected because incompatible child reports were not shown reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated at a decision point.
Rejected because the parent did not make an observable whole-task completion claim with a visible unresolved integrated gap; the run simply ended after stopped work and an empty final response.

Rejected because the retries are visible as stalled workflow retry pressure, but there is not enough evidence that replacement agents lacked inherited checkpoints and repeated a specific prior finding.

candidates.reason: Rejected as downstream of the same fan-out timeout chain; child stops are visible, but the retained corrective boundary is preventing broad retry exhaustion rather than separately premature cancellation.
Rejected because no complete promotable candidate or mutually compatible completed component set existed before closure; only partial implementation pieces were present.
Rejected because no child result or implementation change was merged after integrated verification; the run did not complete integrated verification.
Rejected because no completed delegated implementation is shown as retrievable and then ignored by the parent; the extra implementation-related child was stopped.
Rejected because verifier or critique results were absent as part of the broader stopped workflow and not a separate trapped concrete verifier finding.
Rejected because stopped or stalled child work is part of the retained fan-out exhaustion episode; there is no distinct failed required child with a separate unclaimed takeover opportunity.
Rejected because no concise completed child result is shown available to the parent and then ignored at a decision point.
Rejected because the parent received workflow progress and then stopped work; the problem was excessive fan-out/retries, not waiting blindly without inspection.
Rejected because there is no proven pair of concurrent files claiming overlapping behavior and producing incompatible designs requiring reconciliation.
Rejected because no two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and observing a same-file conflict.
Rejected because no agent is shown replacing source owned or produced by another agent; the late source edit does not prove an overwrite of another actor's module.
Rejected because no required executable or submitted entry point is shown being replaced while another actor owned or used it.
Rejected because no broad cleanup or promotion replaced multiple final outputs or invalidated another agent's final tree.
Rejected because shared workspace writes existed but the concrete realized state problem was environment artifact leakage; no unresolved source collision or provenance conflict is proven.

The configuration probe wrote a home-directory .nshrc that emitted HOME-NSHRC-LOADED. Later unrelated probes and another child observed that output as part of normal executable behavior and the child explicitly identified the file as left by another agent before creating an isolated HOME.
candidates.realized_consequence: Later probes were polluted by a shared HOME startup file and one child had to spend work inspecting and avoiding that contamination before continuing.
candidates.near_match_reason: The adverse artifact was consumed through process environment startup, not through an unresolved source or deliverable write collision in the implementation workspace.
